{{short description|Australian particle physicist (1936–2003)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}}
'''John Gordon Rushbrooke''' (1936–2003) was an Australian [[particle physics|particle physicist]].

The son of Neil and Vera Rushbrooke, with four sisters, Rushbrooke was born in [[Geelong]] in 1936 and was brought up there.<ref name=smh>{{cite web |url=http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2003/10/26/1067103271518.html |title=Explorer of the micro-universe |author=Michael Collins Persse |date=27 October 2003 |website=smh.com.au |publisher=The Sunday Morning Herald |access-date=18 July 2017}}</ref> He attended [[Geelong Grammar School]], where he was at the top of every class.<ref name=smh/>

Rushbrooke went on to [[Trinity College, Perth|Trinity College in Perth]], graduating with a BSc in 1956. This was followed by a master's degree at Australia's first [[cyclotron]], where he began his work as a high-energy physicist.<ref name=smh/> His thesis from the [[University of Melbourne]] was on [[Coulomb]] excitations of the atom.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cat.lib.unimelb.edu.au/search~S6?/aRuschena,+Lydia./aruschena+lydia/-3,-1,0,B/frameset&FF=arushbrooke+john+g&1,1,|title=University of Melbourne /Baillieu S|website=cat.lib.unimelb.edu.au|language=en|access-date=2017-07-18}}</ref>

In 1959 Rushbrooke won a scholarship that took him to [[King's College, Cambridge]].<ref name=smh/> Following work at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] and completion of his PhD, Rushbrooke spent a year at [[CERN]] in Geneva before returning to Cambridge to take up a fellowship at [[Downing College]] as director of studies in physics.<ref name=smh/>

For five years from 1977 he was on leave from his duties at Cambridge, based again at CERN, where he became the spokesperson for the [[UA5 Experiment|UA5 collaboration]].<ref name=smh/> The UA5 experiment searched for [[Centauro event]]s at the [[Proton-Antiproton Collider]], a modification of the [[Super Proton Synchrotron]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1009444/files/CM-P00063814.pdf|title=Decisions of the 32nd Meeting of the Research Board|last=Goldchmidt-Clermont|first=Y.|date=15 February 1979|website=CERN Document Server|access-date=18 July 2017}}</ref>

In 1983 Rushbrooke was promoted to a readership in physics at Cambridge, and in 1991 the university conferred on him a second doctorate.<ref name=smh/> During the 1990s Rushbrooke worked on commercializing technology from scanning techniques developed at CERN.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/john-gordon-rushbrooke|title=John Gordon Rushbrooke Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com|language=en|access-date=2017-07-18}}</ref> He moved to California in 2000 after securing a contract with a major US company.<ref name=smh/>

Rushbrooke died in California in 2003, at the age of 67.
